azure_virtual_machine.properties.storage.text: Specifies the caching mode for the data disk. Allowed values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite.

Specifies the method used to create the data disk. Allowed values: 'FromImage' (create from an image), 'Empty' (create an empty disk), 'Attach' (attach an existing managed disk), 'Copy' (copy from a snapshot or another disk), and 'Restore' (create from a restore point).
Specifies whether the data disk should be deleted or detached when the virtual machine is deleted. Allowed values are 'Delete' or 'Detach'.
Specifies the detach option for a data disk. The only allowed value is 'ForceDetach', which forces the detachment of the disk even if it is currently in use.
The number of IOPS (input/output operations per second) permitted for read/write operations on the managed disk. This setting is applicable only to ultra disks and premium SSD v2 disks.
Specifies the disk throughput in megabytes per second (MBps) for read/write operations, used for Ultra Disk configurations.
The size of the data disk in gigabytes.
The source user image (VHD) for the data disk, specified as an object containing the URI of the virtual hard disk.
The URI of the source VHD blob that the data disk image references, used to create the managed or unmanaged data disk.
Specifies the logical unit number (LUN) for the data disk. This value uniquely identifies the data disk within the virtual machine.
Specifies the action to take when a disk delay is detected. Valid values are 'None' (no automatic action) and 'AutomaticReattach' (automatically reattach the disk).
Indicates whether bursting is enabled for the managed disk. When enabled, the disk can temporarily burst its performance beyond the provisioned limits.
The resource ID of the DiskAccess resource used to configure private endpoint connectivity for the managed disk.
The maximum number of read-only IOPS that the managed disk can support.
The read-only disk throughput limit in MB/s for the managed disk.
The logical sector size of the managed disk in bytes. Allowed values are 512 and 4096.
The maximum number of virtual machines that can share the disk. The minimum allowed value is 1.

Specifies the network access policy for the managed disk. Allowed values are 'AllowAll' (allows public network access), 'AllowPrivate' (restricts access to private networks), and 'DenyAll' (denies all network access).
Indicates whether the managed disk is optimized for frequent attach and detach operations, which can help improve performance for workloads that repeatedly mount and unmount the disk.
Boolean flag that enables the PerformancePlus feature on the managed disk, providing additional IOPS and throughput beyond the baseline. Typically used with Ultra disks.
The performance tier of the Azure managed data disk (e.g., Standard, Premium, or Ultra).
The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed disk with customer-managed keys.
The resource ID of the Azure Disk Encryption Set used to encrypt the managed disk.
Specifies the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed disk with customer-managed keys. Contains a reference to the encryption set resource.

The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed disk. This is a fully qualified Azure resource ID in the format /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/resourceGroups/{resourceGroupName}/providers/Microsoft.Compute/diskEncryptionSets/{encryptionSetName}.

Specifies the encryption type used for the managed disk's security profile in an Azure VM. Allowed values are 'VMGuestStateOnly' (encrypt only the VM guest state), 'DiskWithVMGuestState' (encrypt both the VM guest state and the disk), and 'NonPersistedTPM' (use a non-persisted TPM).
The storage account type for the managed disk. Allowed values are: Standard_LRS, Premium_LRS, StandardSSD_LRS, UltraSSD_LRS, Premium_ZRS, StandardSSD_ZRS, PremiumV2_LRS.

The source disk, snapshot, or image from which this data disk is created. This property is used when creating a disk from an existing resource and contains the resource ID (e.g., '/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/...').
The Azure resource ID of the source resource (for example, a snapshot or managed disk) from which the data disk is created.
Specifies the fault domain alignment strategy for the data disk. Supported values are `Aligned` (strict alignment) and `BestEffortAligned` (best-effort alignment).
Specifies whether the data disk should be detached from the virtual machine. Set to true to detach the disk during an update operation.
Specifies the virtual hard disk settings for an unmanaged data disk, including the URI of the underlying blob storage.
The full Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) of the virtual hard disk (VHD) in Azure Storage that backs the data disk, used for unmanaged disks.
Indicates whether Write Accelerator is enabled for the data disk. Write Accelerator is a feature that improves write latency for managed disks.
The source Azure Key Vault that contains the disk encryption key. This required object must reference the key vault resource ID (typically via the 'id' property) to identify where the key is stored.

The Azure Key Vault that contains the key encryption key. This property holds a reference (resource ID) to the vault where the key is stored, and is required for encrypting the OS disk's encryption key.
The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the OS disk.
The fully qualified Azure resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the OS disk. This references a disk encryption set resource in the same subscription and region.

azure_virtual_machine.properties.virtual.text: The virtual machine scale set that this virtual machine belongs to. This object contains information about the scale set, such as its resource ID, and is present only when the VM is part of a scale set.

azure_virtual_machine.resources.properti.text: Indicates whether the extension handler version should be automatically upgraded to a newer minor version when available. Set to true to enable automatic upgrades, or false to disable.
Indicates whether the virtual machine extension is automatically upgraded by Azure when a newer version of the extension is available.
A user-defined value that forces the extension to re-provision even if its configuration hasn't changed. Set a new value to trigger an update on the next deployment.
The runtime instance view of the virtual machine, which includes status details such as the machine's power state, provisioning state, disk status, and other health information.

The statuses field contains a list of InstanceViewStatus objects representing the current status of the virtual machine, such as its provisioning state (e.g., Succeeded, Failed) and power state (e.g., Running, Stopped). Each status includes details like code, level, display status, and time of the status.
The status code for the virtual machine instance view status, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'PowerState/running'.
The human-readable, localized status text for the resource, such as 'Provisioning succeeded' or 'Running', used for display in the Azure portal.
The severity level of the status. Possible values are Info, Warning, and Error.
Provides additional information about the status, such as error details or a description of the current state. Often used to convey the underlying reason for the status code.
The timestamp when the status was last reported, in date-time format.
The status code for the substatus entry, indicating the specific condition represented by the substatus.
The human-readable status message for this sub-status, providing a display-friendly description of the current status condition.
The severity level of the substatus, indicating the type of status message. Allowed values are Info, Warning, and Error.
The status message text associated with the substatus.
The timestamp when the substatus was recorded, typically in ISO 8601 format.
The version of the extension type handler that is installed on the virtual machine, as reported in the instance view.

Sensitive configuration for the virtual machine extension. These settings are encrypted by Azure and not returned by the API; use this field for secrets and other protected data that should not be stored in plaintext.

Protected settings for a VM extension that are retrieved from Azure Key Vault. This object typically includes the Key Vault reference containing the secret URL, enabling sensitive settings to be stored securely and referenced instead of being passed directly.

The URI of a Key Vault secret that contains the protected settings value. The URL must be a valid Azure Key Vault secret reference, e.g., https://<vault-name>.vault.azure.net/secrets/<secret-name>/<secret-version>.
Specifies the source Key Vault that contains the secret for protected settings. This object references the Key Vault resource by its ID in the 'id' property.
The Azure resource ID of the Key Vault that contains the secret referenced in the protected settings.
A list of extension names that must be provisioned before this extension is provisioned. This property is used to control the order of extension provisioning on the VM.
The current provisioning state of the virtual machine, such as 'Succeeded', 'Updating', 'Failed', or 'Canceled'. This reflects the progress of resource creation or update operations.
The publisher of the image used to create the virtual machine, such as 'Canonical' or 'MicrosoftWindowsServer'. This is part of the image reference within the VM properties.
Specifies the version of the extension handler that will be used to execute the extension. For example, '1.0' or '2.0'.

azure_virtual_machine_diagnostic_run_com.text: The status code for the instance view status, indicating the state of the diagnostic run command.
The severity level of the instance view status. Possible values are 'Info', 'Warning', and 'Error'.
The message that provides additional details about the status of the diagnostic run command, such as error information or execution progress.
The timestamp when the status was recorded, in ISO 8601 format.
The value of the parameter to pass to the diagnostic run command.
The name of the protected parameter to pass to the run command.
The value of a protected parameter, used to hold sensitive information such as passwords or keys that are passed to the diagnostic run command.

azure_virtual_machine_extension.properti.text: The machine-readable status code for the extension instance view status, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'ProvisioningState/failed'.
The localized, human-readable status message displayed for the extension instance view status.
The severity level of the status, indicating whether it is informational, a warning, or an error. Allowed values: Info, Warning, Error.
A human-readable message providing additional details about the extension's status, as part of the instance view statuses.
The time at which the status was recorded, typically in ISO 8601 format.
The machine-readable code representing the specific substatus condition, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or an error code.
The short, human-readable label for the substatus, typically providing the localized status message.
The severity level of the substatus, indicating whether it is informational, a warning, or an error. Allowed values: Info, Warning, Error.
The detailed message associated with the substatus of the virtual machine extension instance view, providing additional context or error information about the extension's health or status.
The timestamp when the substatus was reported.
The Key Vault that holds the protected settings. This is a reference to the vault (e.g., its resource ID) and is required when supplying protected settings via a Key Vault.

azure_virtual_machine_run_command.proper.text: The status code of the run command instance view, representing the current state (e.g., 'ProvisioningState/succeeded').
The localized, human-readable status message for the run command instance, providing a user-friendly description of the current state (e.g., 'Provisioning succeeded' or 'Failed').
The severity level of the status, one of Info, Warning, or Error.
The human-readable status message associated with the instance view of the virtual machine run command.
The timestamp when the status was observed, typically in ISO 8601 format.
The name of the parameter to be passed to the run command. This name is used as the key for the parameter value.
The value of a parameter used by the virtual machine run command.
The name of the protected parameter, serving as the key in the key-value pair.
The value of the protected parameter. This value is sensitive and should be kept secret.

azure_virtual_machine_scale_set.identity.text: The client ID (application ID) of the user-assigned managed identity associated with the virtual machine scale set.
The principal ID (object ID in Azure AD) of the user-assigned identity assigned to the virtual machine scale set.

azure_virtual_machine_scale_set.properti.text: Configuration for the dedicated host group that the virtual machine scale set will be assigned to. This object contains the resource ID of the host group.
The default action to take when a lifecycle hook is triggered. Allowed values are 'Approve' or 'Reject'.

The type of the lifecycle hook. Allowed values are 'UpgradeAutoOSScheduling' (when an automatic OS upgrade is scheduled) and 'UpgradeAutoOSRollingBatchStarting' (when a rolling batch starts for an automatic OS upgrade).
The maximum duration (in ISO 8601 format, e.g., 'PT5M') that the platform waits for all lifecycle hooks to complete before proceeding with the scale-set operation.

The resource ID of an existing proximity placement group to place the virtual machine scale set instances in. This optional configuration can reduce network latency between VMs for latency-sensitive workloads.
The name of the virtual machine size, such as 'Standard_D2s_v3'.
Specifies the URI (typically a SAS URI) of the configuration file for the gallery application. This configuration file is downloaded and executed on the virtual machine.

Indicates whether the gallery application should be automatically upgraded to the latest version when a new version is released. If true, the virtual machine scale set automatically applies upgrades for this application.
Specifies the order in which the gallery applications are installed. Lower values are installed first.
The resource ID of the gallery application version to be installed on the virtual machine scale set.

Indicates whether a failure to install or configure the gallery application on the VM should be treated as a failure of the VM deployment, causing the VM to be marked as failed. If true, any error during application provisioning will fail the deployment; if false, such failures are logged but do not fail the deployment.
The capacity reservation group to associate with the virtual machine scale set. This allows the scale set's instances to use pre-reserved compute capacity.
The properties of the extension, including publisher, type, type handler version, settings, and protected settings.
Indicates whether the extension handler version will be automatically upgraded to a newer minor version when a new version becomes available.
Indicates whether the extension should be automatically upgraded by the platform when a newer extension version is available.

A string value used to force the extension to be re-applied even if the extension configuration has not changed. Changing this value (e.g., to a new timestamp) triggers a re-provisioning of the extension on all instances.
Sensitive, encrypted configuration settings for the extension (e.g., credentials or keys). These settings are not returned in read operations and are stored securely.
Specifies a reference to a Key Vault secret that contains the protected settings for the extension, instead of providing them inline. The object typically includes the source vault and secret URL.
The URL of the Key Vault secret that contains the protected settings for the extension. This URL typically points to a secret version, e.g., https://myvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/mysecret/version.
The Key Vault resource that contains the secret used to protect the extension settings. This is a reference to an existing Key Vault, identified by its resource ID.
Specifies the resource ID of the key vault from which the protected settings are taken.
Specifies a list of extension names that must be provisioned before this extension. Enables ordering of extensions within the scale set.
The current provisioning state of the extension in the Azure VM scale set, indicating whether deployment has succeeded or failed.
The name of the publisher of the virtual machine extension, such as Microsoft.Azure.Extensions or Microsoft.Compute. This is required when configuring an extension.
The public configuration settings for the VM extension. The schema varies by extension type; refer to the specific extension's documentation for expected keys and values.

Indicates whether to suppress extension failures. When set to true, a failure in this extension does not cause the virtual machine scale set deployment or update to fail, and the failure is not surfaced as a deployment error.
The type of the extension, such as CustomScript or IaaSAntimalware, which identifies the extension handler to use.
The version of the extension handler. Specifies which version of the extension type to use, such as '1.0' or '2.0'.

The type of the virtual machine extension, such as 'CustomScriptExtension' or 'DscExtension'. This value identifies the extension handler and works with the publisher and version to define extension behavior.
The name of the network interface configuration. Must be unique within the virtual machine scale set.

Specifies the auxiliary mode for the network interface. Allowed values are 'None' (default), 'AcceleratedConnections' for accelerated networking connections, and 'Floating' for floating IP configurations.

Specifies the SKU for the auxiliary network interface. Allowed values are None, A1, A2, A4, and A8, where None indicates no auxiliary network is used and the A-series values represent different sizes of the auxiliary NIC.
Specifies the action to take on the network interface when the virtual machine is deleted. Allowed values are 'Delete' (delete the network interface) and 'Detach' (detach and retain it).

Indicates whether to disable TCP state tracking on the network interface. When true, TCP state tracking is disabled, which can reduce overhead for high-throughput workloads but may impact features that rely on stateful inspection.
DNS settings for the network interface configuration, such as custom DNS servers and the internal DNS name label applied to instances in the scale set.
The list of DNS server IP addresses assigned to the network interface.

Indicates whether accelerated networking is enabled for the network interface configuration. When enabled, this allows the VM to use Azure's accelerated networking feature (SR-IOV) for improved network performance.
Specifies whether FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) networking is enabled for this network interface configuration.

Enable or disable IP forwarding on this network interface. When enabled, the VM can forward packets destined for other IP addresses, which is useful for network virtual appliances or routing scenarios. Default is false.
A list of IP configurations for this network interface. Each configuration specifies private IP allocation, subnet, and optional public IP or load balancer backend pool membership.
The name of the IP configuration.
The properties of the IP configuration in a virtual machine scale set network interface, including subnet, primary, public IP configuration, and load balancer pool references.

Specifies the list of Application Gateway backend address pool references (resource IDs) to which this IP configuration is associated. When defined, instances in the scale set using this IP configuration are added to the specified backend pools, enabling the Application Gateway to route traffic to them.
The resource ID of the application gateway backend address pool associated with this IP configuration.
A list of application security groups to which this IP configuration is associated. Each item contains the resource ID of an Azure application security group.
The resource ID of the application security group (ASG) that this IP configuration should be associated with.
List of references to load balancer backend address pools that this IP configuration should be associated with. Used to attach the scale set instances to backend pools of an Azure Load Balancer.
The Azure resource ID of the load balancer backend address pool to associate with this IP configuration.
A list of references to load balancer inbound NAT pools associated with this IP configuration. Each item links the IP configuration to a specific inbound NAT pool from the load balancer.
The Azure resource ID of the load balancer inbound NAT pool to associate with the IP configuration.
Indicates whether this IP configuration is the primary one for the network interface. Only one IP configuration can be the primary per network interface.
Specifies the version of the private IP address assigned to the IP configuration. Allowed values are 'IPv4' or 'IPv6'.
Configuration for the public IP address associated with this IP configuration in the network interface of a VM scale set.
The name of the public IP address configuration associated with the network interface's IP configuration in the virtual machine scale set.

Specifies whether the public IP address is deleted or detached when the associated virtual machine is deleted. Valid values are 'Delete' (the IP is removed) and 'Detach' (the IP is kept and becomes a standalone resource).
DNS settings for the public IP address associated with the IP configuration. Typically includes a domain name label that is used to derive the fully qualified domain name (FQDN).
The domain name label for the public IP address. Combined with the regional DNS zone, it forms the fully qualified domain name. If set, an A record is created for this public IP in Azure DNS.
Specifies the scope for reusing the domain name label. Allowed values are TenantReuse, SubscriptionReuse, ResourceGroupReuse, and NoReuse.
The idle timeout for the public IP address in minutes, which controls how long a connection is kept open without activity. Valid values are between 4 and 30 minutes.
A list of IP tags associated with the public IP address. Each IP tag includes a tag type (e.g., FirstPartyUsage) and a tag value, used to categorize or apply metadata to the public IP.
The type of the IP tag. Common types include 'FirstPartyUsage' and 'RoutingPreference'.
The value for an IP tag in the public IP address configuration. It pairs with the IP tag type to apply a classification to the public IP address.
The IP version of the public IP address. Allowed values are IPv4 or IPv6.
Defines the Public IP Prefix to use for the public IP address associated with the network interface. When specified, the public IP address is allocated from this prefix.
The Azure resource ID of the public IP prefix to associate with the public IP configuration.
The SKU of the public IP address, which defines its performance tier and features. Contains the name (Basic or Standard) and optionally the tier (Regional or Global).
The SKU name for the public IP address configuration. Allowed values are 'Basic' and 'Standard'.
The tier of the public IP address SKU, indicating whether the public IP is regional (Regional) or global (Global).
A set of key-value pairs to be applied as tags on the public IP address created from this configuration, used for resource organization and management.
Specifies the subnet in a virtual network where the IP configuration is attached. This is typically an object containing the 'id' of the subnet resource.
The network security group (NSG) to associate with the network interface. It specifies the NSG that controls traffic for the network interface in the VM scale set.
The Azure resource ID of the network security group to associate with the network interface configuration.
Specifies whether this network interface configuration is the primary network interface for the virtual machine scale set instances. Only one network interface configuration can be marked as primary.
The SSH public key data, typically the contents of a public key file (e.g., 'ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2E...'). This key is used for authentication to the Linux VM.
The full path on the Linux VM where the SSH public key is stored, typically the authorized_keys file for a specific user (e.g., /home/azureuser/.ssh/authorized_keys).
Specifies the Key Vault that contains the certificates used in the secrets for the virtual machine scale set's OS profile.
The resource ID of the Azure Key Vault that contains the secrets.
Specifies the list of certificates to install from the referenced Azure Key Vault. Each item contains the certificate URL and, for Windows, the certificate store to place the certificate in.
Specifies the certificate store on the virtual machine where the certificate should be added. This is used for Windows VMs; for Linux VMs, this value is ignored.
The URL of the certificate stored in Azure Key Vault, referencing the secret version of the certificate to be installed on the virtual machine.
The name of the Windows component to configure. For additional unattend content in a virtual machine scale set, this must be Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup.
The base64-encoded XML content that is added to the unattend.xml file for Windows configuration.
The Windows unattend pass name. The only supported value is OobeSystem.
Specifies the name of the Windows unattend content setting. Valid values are 'AutoLogon' and 'FirstLogonCommands'.
The URL to the certificate used for the WinRM HTTPS listener. The certificate must be stored in Azure Key Vault.
Specifies the protocol of the Windows Remote Management (WinRM) listener. Allowed values are 'Http' and 'Https'.
Configuration for Scheduled Events on the virtual machine scale set, including settings for OS image notifications and termination notifications.

Specifies the profile for OS image notifications within the scheduled events configuration of a virtual machine scale set. This optional object defines settings for how and when notifications about OS image updates are delivered.
The profile for configuring terminate notifications, which lets you enable termination notification and specify the notification timeout for scale-in events in Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets.
The caching mode for the data disk, controlling host caching behavior. Valid values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite.

Specifies how the data disk should be created. Allowed values are: FromImage (use the image), Empty (create an empty disk), Attach (attach an existing managed disk), Copy (create from a snapshot), and Restore (create from a restore point).
Specifies the action to take on the data disk when the VM is deleted. Allowed values: Delete or Detach.
The number of input/output operations per second (IOPS) allowed for the managed data disk. Use this to tune disk performance beyond the default baseline.
The disk throughput in megabytes per second (MB/s) for read/write operations, applicable to Ultra SSD data disks in the scale set.
Specifies the size of the data disk in gigabytes.
The logical unit number (LUN) for the data disk. This specifies the slot within the virtual machine where the disk will be attached, and must be unique among all data disks on the VM.
Specifies the managed disk settings for the data disk, including the storage account type and encryption configuration.
Specifies the action to take on a disk when a disk delay is detected. Allowed values are 'None' and 'AutomaticReattach'.
Specifies whether bursting is enabled for the managed disk. When enabled, the disk can burst beyond its provisioned performance limits.
The resource ID of the disk access resource to use for the managed disk, enabling private endpoint connectivity.
The number of IOPS allowed for read-only operations on the managed disk. Used for disk types that support separate read and write IOPS limits, such as Ultra SSDs.
The logical sector size in bytes for the managed disk. Allowed values are 512 (default) and 4096.
The maximum number of virtual machines that can share this managed disk. Value must be at least 1.

The network access policy for the managed disk. Allowed values: AllowAll (allows all network access), AllowPrivate (allows access only from private endpoints), and DenyAll (denies all network access).

When true, enables Performance Plus on the managed disk, allowing it to achieve higher IOPS and throughput limits than its baseline for an additional cost. This feature is only available in certain regions and for specific disk sizes.
The performance tier of the managed disk, which determines its IOPS and throughput (e.g., P10, P20 for premium disks).
Specifies the Disk Encryption Set used to encrypt this managed data disk at rest with customer-managed keys. The object should provide the resource ID of the encryption set.
The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed disk.
Security configuration for the managed data disk, including encryption settings and associated disk encryption set.
Specifies the Disk Encryption Set (DES) resource ID used for encrypting the managed disk with customer-managed keys. Provide the fully qualified resource ID of the Disk Encryption Set.
Specifies the resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed data disk.

Specifies the security encryption type for the managed disk. Allowed values are VMGuestStateOnly (encrypts only the VM guest state), DiskWithVMGuestState (encrypts both the disk and the VM guest state), and NonPersistedTPM (uses non-persisted TPM for encryption).
Specifies the storage account type for the managed disk. Allowed values: Standard_LRS, Premium_LRS, StandardSSD_LRS, UltraSSD_LRS, Premium_ZRS, StandardSSD_ZRS, PremiumV2_LRS.
The user-defined name of the data disk in the virtual machine scale set's storage profile.

Specifies how the data disk's fault domain is aligned with the scale set's VM fault domains. `Aligned` ensures the disk is placed in the same fault domain as the virtual machine, while `BestEffortAligned` attempts to align it but does not guarantee the placement.
The Azure resource ID of the Disk Encryption Set (DES) used to encrypt the managed OS disk.
The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the OS disk.

azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_extensio.text: Specifies the Key Vault resource that contains the secret for the protected settings. The object typically includes the Azure resource ID of the Key Vault.

azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vm.ident.text: The client ID (GUID) of the user-assigned managed identity, used to identify it when requesting tokens.
The principal ID of the user-assigned identity assigned to the virtual machine scale set VM.

azure_virtual_machine_scale_set_vm.prope.text: Specifies the capacity reservation group to associate with the virtual machine scale set VM. This allows the VM to use reserved capacity from the specified group.

The encryption settings for the disk, as observed in the instance view. Each object represents the encryption configuration applied to this disk, typically including encryption status and key references.
The disk encryption key used for encrypting the disk, containing a reference to the Azure Key Vault secret (secret URL and source vault).
The secret URL of the disk encryption key in the Key Vault. This URL points to the secret containing the encryption key used for disk encryption.
Specifies the Azure Key Vault that contains the disk encryption key used for encrypting the disk.
The resource ID of the Key Vault containing the disk encryption key.
Indicates whether encryption is enabled for the disk.
Represents the Key Encryption Key (KEK) used to wrap the disk encryption key. Includes the key URL and the source vault reference.
The URL of the key encryption key (KEK) used to wrap the disk encryption key.
The Key Vault that contains the key encryption key used for disk encryption.
The Azure resource ID of the Key Vault that contains the key encryption key.
A list of statuses reported for the disk, with each status containing details such as code, level, display status, and message.
The code of the disk status, indicating the disk's current state in the instance view (e.g., 'Attached' or 'Detached').
The human-readable status of the disk, such as 'Healthy' or 'Unhealthy'.
The severity level of the disk status. Possible values are Info, Warning, and Error.
A human-readable message that provides additional details about the disk status.
The timestamp (in UTC) indicating when the disk status was last reported or updated.
The storage alignment status of the disk. Possible values are 'Aligned' and 'Unaligned'.
The name of the virtual machine extension as reported in the instance view.
The list of statuses for the extension instance view, including status code, level, display status, message, and time.
The status code for the extension's current state, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'ProvisioningState/failed'.
The human-readable status description for this instance view status, such as 'Provisioning succeeded' or 'Provisioning failed'. It is the localized display equivalent of the status code.
The severity level of the status, indicating the impact or urgency. Possible values are Info, Warning, and Error.
A human-readable message providing additional details about the extension status.
The timestamp, as a string, when the status was reported or last updated.
The list of sub-statuses for the extension instance view, providing additional status information beyond the primary status.
The level of the status, which indicates the severity. Possible values are Info, Warning, and Error.
The status message, providing additional information about the extension's condition or substatus.
The time when the substatus was recorded, typically in ISO 8601 format.
The type of the virtual machine extension, specifying the publisher and extension type (e.g., Microsoft.Azure.Extensions.CustomScript).
The version number of the extension handler running on the VM instance.
The status code for the VM instance, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'PowerState/running'. This code identifies the specific status condition.
The human-readable display status of the virtual machine instance, such as 'Provisioning succeeded' or 'Running'.
The severity level of the status. Possible values are Info, Warning, and Error.

A human-readable message providing additional details about the status. In Azure instance view statuses, this field contains the message text for the corresponding status code, such as the reason for a provisioning state or health state.
The timestamp indicating when the status was last updated, formatted as an ISO 8601 date-time string.
The status of the extension handler, containing properties such as code, level (e.g., Info, Warning, Error), displayStatus, message, and time.
The machine-readable status code for the extension handler, such as 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'ProvisioningState/failed'.
The human-readable status text for the extension handler status, such as 'Provisioning succeeded' or 'Provisioning failed'.
Indicates the severity level of the status. Possible values are 'Info', 'Warning', and 'Error'.
The status message providing additional details about the current state of the extension handler. This often contains error details or informational text corresponding to the status code.
The timestamp when the extension handler status was reported.
The type of the extension handler, such as Microsoft.Compute.CustomScriptExtension.
The version of the extension handler type installed on the virtual machine.
The status code for the VM agent, typically indicating its provisioning state (e.g., 'ProvisioningState/succeeded' or 'ProvisioningState/failed').
A human-readable label that describes the current status of the VM agent, suitable for display to users.
The severity level of the status: Info, Warning, or Error.
The message associated with the VM agent status, providing additional details about the condition indicated by the status code.
The time at which the status was reported by the VM agent.
The name of the network interface configuration. This name is used to identify the NIC configuration within the network profile of the VM scale set instance.
Specifies the auxiliary mode of the network interface configuration. Allowed values: `None`, `AcceleratedConnections`, and `Floating`.
The SKU for the auxiliary mode of the network interface configuration. Allowed values are 'None', 'A1', 'A2', 'A4', and 'A8'.

Specifies whether the network interface is deleted or detached when the virtual machine scale set VM is deleted. Allowed values: 'Delete' (delete the NIC) and 'Detach' (keep the NIC, remove association).

Whether TCP state tracking is disabled on this network interface configuration. Set to true to disable the Azure platform's TCP state tracking, typically for network virtual appliances that manage their own connection state.
DNS settings for the network interface configuration, used to specify custom DNS server IP addresses for the VMSS instance's network interface.
Specifies the list of custom DNS server IP addresses to use for the network interface.
The DSCP configuration associated with this network interface. This is a reference object containing the resource ID of an existing DSCP configuration.
The resource ID of the DSCP (Differentiated Services Code Point) configuration associated with this network interface configuration.
Indicates whether accelerated networking is enabled on the network interface. When enabled, this enables single root I/O virtualization (SR-IOV) for the VM, which can improve network performance.
Whether to enable FPGA-based network acceleration on this network interface. When true, the interface uses FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) capabilities to offload network processing.
Enables IP forwarding on this network interface, allowing the VM to forward traffic from other network interfaces or sources, commonly used for network virtual appliances.

A list of IP configurations for this network interface configuration. Each IP configuration defines the private IP address, subnet, and optional public IP address for the virtual machine scale set VM.
The name of the IP configuration. This name must be unique within the network interface.

A list of references to backend address pools of an Azure Application Gateway. Each entry is a SubResource containing the resource ID of the backend pool. The IP configuration is associated with these pools so that the VM can receive traffic routed by the application gateway.
The Azure resource ID of the Application Gateway backend address pool associated with this IP configuration.

The list of Application Security Groups (ASGs) associated with the IP configuration. Each object references an ASG by its resource ID, enabling the grouping of virtual machines for security policy enforcement.
The Azure resource ID of the application security group to associate with the IP configuration.

Specifies the backend address pools of a load balancer to which this IP configuration is associated. In Azure, this is typically an array of references (resource IDs) to the load balancer's backend address pools.
The resource ID of the load balancer backend address pool to which the IP configuration should be associated.
Indicates whether this IP configuration is the primary configuration for the network interface. When true, this configuration is the primary IP configuration.
The private IP address version for the IP configuration, either IPv4 or IPv6.
Specifies whether the public IP address is deleted or detached when the VM is deleted. Allowed values: 'Delete' (delete the public IP) and 'Detach' (retain the public IP, but detach it from the VM).
Configuration for DNS settings on the public IP address, including domain name label and fully qualified domain name (FQDN).
The domain name label for the DNS settings of the public IP address. This label is used to construct the FQDN as <label>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com.

Specifies the scope of domain name label reuse. Allowed values are TenantReuse, SubscriptionReuse, ResourceGroupReuse, and NoReuse, which indicate whether the label can be reused at the tenant, subscription, resource group, or not at all.
The idle timeout in minutes for the public IP address. This specifies how long a connection can remain idle before being closed by Azure; valid values are typically between 4 and 30 minutes.
A list of IP tags to associate with the public IP address. Each IP tag is used to classify traffic for Microsoft and partner services, typically containing a tag type and a tag value.
The unique identifier of the first-party service tag associated with this IP tag.
The type of the IP tag, which indicates the category or purpose of the tag (e.g., 'FirstPartyUsage' for first-party services).
The value of the IP tag. This is paired with the IP tag type to specify a classification for the public IP address, such as routing preference or usage category.
The IP version of the public IP address. Valid values are 'IPv4' and 'IPv6'.
Specifies the public IP address allocation method. Allowed values are 'Dynamic' (the IP address can change) and 'Static' (a fixed IP address is assigned).
The public IP prefix resource to associate with the public IP address. This allows the IP address to be allocated from a predefined range.
The resource ID of the public IP prefix to associate with this public IP address configuration.
The SKU (stock keeping unit) for the public IP address configuration, defining the pricing tier and available features.
The SKU name for the public IP address. Allowed values are Basic and Standard.
The tier of the public IP address SKU. Allowed values are 'Regional' or 'Global'.
A map of key-value pairs used to tag the public IP address configuration for management and organization purposes.
A reference to the subnet resource within the virtual network to which this IP configuration is attached.
The Azure resource ID of the subnet.
The network security group (NSG) associated with this network interface configuration within the virtual machine scale set.
The resource ID of the network security group associated with the network interface configuration.
Specifies whether this network interface is the primary network interface for the virtual machine. Only one network interface configuration in the scale set can be marked as primary.
The configuration properties of the network interface, including its IP configurations and whether it is the primary network interface.
Specifies whether the network interface should be deleted or detached when the VM is deleted. 'Delete' removes the NIC, while 'Detach' keeps it but removes the association.
Indicates whether this is the primary network interface for the virtual machine. One network interface must be marked as primary.
Specifies the auxiliary mode for the network interface configuration. Possible values are: None, AcceleratedConnections, and Floating.

Specifies the auxiliary SKU for the network interface, which determines the auxiliary network capability. Allowed values are None (no auxiliary SKU) and A1, A2, A4, A8, with higher values indicating increased auxiliary network configuration.
Determines whether the network interface is deleted or detached when the virtual machine is deleted. Allowed values: 'Delete' or 'Detach'.

Indicates whether TCP state tracking is disabled for the IP configuration. When set to true, the network interface does not track TCP connection state, which can be useful for asymmetric routing scenarios.
DNS settings for the network interface, including DNS servers and internal DNS name label.
The list of DNS server IP addresses to apply to this network interface.

Enables accelerated networking on the network interface, which uses Single Root I/O Virtualization (SR-IOV) to provide higher networking performance and lower latency. Set to true to enable, false to disable.
Whether to enable FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) acceleration on this network interface configuration. Set to true only for VM sizes that support FPGA-accelerated networking.

Indicates whether IP forwarding is enabled on this network interface. When enabled, the virtual machine can forward packets not addressed to itself, which is useful for scenarios such as routing or network virtual appliances.
Specifies the IP configurations for the network interface. Each IP configuration defines settings such as subnet, private IP address allocation, and associated public IP address.
The specific configuration properties for this IP configuration, including settings such as the subnet, private IP address allocation, and any associated load balancer backend pools.
Specifies the list of application gateway backend address pools associated with this IP configuration. Each object in the list represents a reference to a backend address pool resource.
The resource ID of the application gateway backend address pool.
Specifies the application security groups that the network interface IP configuration belongs to. Each item contains the resource ID of an application security group.
The Azure resource ID of the application security group to associate with the IP configuration.

Specifies the list of load balancer backend address pools to which this IP configuration is assigned, enabling the virtual machine to receive inbound traffic from a load balancer. Each item is a reference to an existing backend pool in the associated load balancer.
The Azure resource ID of the load balancer backend address pool.
List of references to load balancer inbound NAT pools associated with this IP configuration. Each element specifies a load balancer inbound NAT pool to use for port forwarding or traffic routing.
The unique resource ID of the load balancer inbound NAT pool.
Specifies whether this IP configuration is the primary IP configuration for the network interface. Only one IP configuration per network interface can be set as primary.
The IP version of the private IP address, either IPv4 or IPv6.
The public IP address configuration for this IP configuration, used to define settings for the public IP address assigned to the network interface in the virtual machine scale set.
The name of the public IP address configuration within the IP configuration of a network interface.

Specifies the behavior for the public IP address when the VM is deleted. Allowed values are "Delete" (the public IP is deleted along with the VM) and "Detach" (the public IP is detached and remains in the subscription).
DNS settings for the public IP address, including the domain name label, fully qualified domain name (FQDN), and reverse FQDN.

The domain name label for the public IP address. The concatenation of this label and the regionalized DNS zone forms the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the public IP, which enables an A record to be created in Azure DNS.
The scope in which the domain name label can be reused. Allowed values are: TenantReuse, SubscriptionReuse, ResourceGroupReuse, and NoReuse.
The number of minutes that a connection to the public IP address can remain idle before it is terminated by Azure.
A list of IP tags for the public IP address. Each tag is an object containing a tag type and a tag value.
The ID of a first-party Azure service tag (such as a tag for Azure Storage or SQL) that this IP tag associates with the public IP address.
Specifies the type of the IP tag applied to the public IP address. In Azure, this is commonly set to 'FirstPartyUsage' for Microsoft-assigned tags, but custom tag types are also allowed.
The value of the IP tag, such as 'SQL' or 'Storage', which classifies the public IP address according to the tag type.
The version of the public IP address assigned to this IP configuration. Allowed values are IPv4 or IPv6.
Specifies the public IP prefix from which the public IP address is allocated. This is a reference to a public IP prefix resource.
The Azure resource ID of the public IP prefix to associate with this public IP configuration.
The SKU of the public IP address, defining its tier and performance characteristics.
The name of the public IP address SKU. Allowed values are 'Basic' and 'Standard'.
Specifies the tier for the public IP address SKU. Allowed values are 'Regional' and 'Global'.
A mapping of user-defined key-value pairs to attach to the public IP address in this configuration. These tags can be used for categorizing and organizing Azure resources.
Specifies the subnet to which the IP configuration is attached. This is a reference object containing the resource ID of the subnet within a virtual network.
The fully qualified Azure resource ID of the subnet to which this IP configuration is attached.
The network security group (NSG) to associate with this network interface configuration. This is a reference to an existing NSG resource, typically specified via its resource ID.
The resource ID of the network security group associated with the network interface configuration.
Indicates whether this network interface is the primary NIC for the virtual machine scale set VM. When multiple network interfaces are configured, one must be marked as primary.
The SSH public key data, typically the contents of a public key file in PEM format, used for authenticating to the virtual machine.
The full path on the Linux VM where the SSH public key is placed, typically ending in .ssh/authorized_keys for a specific user.
The Azure Key Vault that contains the certificates to be installed. Each secret in the OS profile must specify a source vault, and the certificates are referenced by their URLs within that vault.
The Azure resource ID of the Key Vault that contains the secrets.
A list of Key Vault certificates to be installed on the virtual machine. Each item references a certificate URL in Azure Key Vault.
The name of the certificate store on the Windows virtual machine where the certificate is added, such as 'My' or 'Root'. This is used when installing certificates from Azure Key Vault.
The URL of the certificate in the Azure Key Vault, including the certificate version. This URL identifies the certificate to install on the virtual machine.
The name of the Windows component to configure during unattended installation. The only allowed value is 'Microsoft-Windows-Shell-Setup'.
Specifies the XML formatted content that is added to the unattend.xml file for the Windows configuration.
The name of the Windows unattend pass for the additional unattended content. The allowed value is 'OobeSystem', which specifies the Out-of-Box Experience pass.
Specifies the name of the additional Unattended Content setting. Allowed values: AutoLogon, FirstLogonCommands.
The URL of the certificate in Azure Key Vault used for the HTTPS WinRM listener on the virtual machine.
Specifies the protocol used by the WinRM listener. Allowed values are 'Http' and 'Https'.
Specifies the caching requirements for the data disk. Possible values are None, ReadOnly, and ReadWrite.

Specifies how the data disk should be created. Allowed values are `FromImage` (use the data disk from the image), `Empty` (create a new blank disk), `Attach` (attach an existing managed disk), `Copy` (create the disk by copying from an existing disk or snapshot), and `Restore` (create the disk from a restore point).
Specifies the behavior of the data disk when the VM is deleted. When set to 'Delete', the disk is deleted along with the VM; when set to 'Detach', the disk is detached and retained.
Specifies the detach option for the data disk. The only supported value is 'ForceDetach', which allows detaching the disk even if it is currently in use or has pending operations.
The number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) that the disk can support for both read and write operations. This is configurable for certain disk types, such as Ultra disks.
The maximum read/write throughput in megabytes per second (MB/s) that the data disk can sustain. This value is used to define the performance tier of the disk.
Specifies the image reference for the data disk, containing the URI to a VHD in a storage account. Used when the disk is created from an image (createOption = 'FromImage').
The URI of the virtual hard disk (VHD) blob used as the image for the data disk. This applies to unmanaged disks, where the image is referenced by its blob storage URI.
The Logical Unit Number (LUN) assigned to the data disk. This value uniquely identifies the disk within the virtual machine and is used by the operating system to address the disk.
The action to take when a disk delay is detected. Allowed values are 'None' (no action) and 'AutomaticReattach' (automatically reattach the disk).
Whether performance bursting is enabled for the managed disk, allowing it to exceed its provisioned performance limits temporarily.
Specifies the Azure resource ID of the DiskAccess resource to associate with the managed disk for enabling private endpoint access to the disk.
The provisioned read-only IOPS limit for the managed disk, expressed in operations per second. This value applies to scenarios where the disk is used in a read-only or shared configuration.

The maximum read throughput, in MB/s, that the managed disk can support when mounted in read-only mode. This performance limit applies to certain disk types (e.g., Ultra disks or Premium SSD v2) within the VMSS VM's data disk configuration.
The maximum number of VMs that can share the disk. The value must be at least 1.

The network access policy for the managed data disk. Allowed values are 'AllowAll' (allow all network access), 'AllowPrivate' (allow only private network access), and 'DenyAll' (deny all network access).

Boolean flag indicating whether the managed disk is optimized for frequent attach/detach operations. When true, the disk is configured to reduce the time for attaching and detaching, which is useful for scenarios like cluster failover.
Specifies whether to enable Azure Managed Disk Performance Plus, which provides higher IOPS and throughput limits on the disk for an additional cost.
Specifies the performance tier of the managed disk (e.g., P10, E10).
Specifies the customer-managed disk encryption set to use for encrypting this managed data disk. Provide the resource ID of the disk encryption set in the 'id' property.
The resource ID of the disk encryption set associated with the managed disk.
The security profile of the managed data disk, used to configure disk-level security options such as Trusted Launch or confidential VM disk encryption.
The disk encryption set used to encrypt this managed disk at rest using customer-managed keys.
The resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed disk.

Specifies the security encryption type for the managed disk. Allowed values: VMGuestStateOnly (encrypts only the VM guest state), DiskWithVMGuestState (encrypts both the disk and the VM guest state), NonPersistedTPM (uses a non-persisted TPM).
Specifies the storage account type for the managed disk. Allowed values are Standard_LRS, Premium_LRS, StandardSSD_LRS, UltraSSD_LRS, Premium_ZRS, StandardSSD_ZRS, and PremiumV2_LRS.
The Azure resource ID of the source resource used to create the data disk, such as a managed disk, snapshot, or image.

Specifies the fault domain alignment mode for the data disk. Possible values are 'Aligned' (disk is placed in the same fault domain as the VM) and 'BestEffortAligned' (alignment is attempted but not guaranteed).
Specifies whether the data disk should be detached from the virtual machine instead of being deleted when the VM is deleted. Set to true to detach the disk, false to delete it with the VM.
The virtual hard disk (VHD) settings for the data disk, typically containing the URI of the VHD blob that backs the disk when using unmanaged storage.
The URI of the virtual hard disk (VHD) in Azure Storage, specifying the blob location for the data disk.
Specifies whether write accelerator is enabled for this data disk.
A reference to the Azure Key Vault that stores the disk encryption key secret used for encrypting the OS disk.
The Key Vault that contains the key encryption key used for disk encryption.
The resource ID of the Azure Disk Encryption Set used to encrypt the OS disk of the scale set VM.
The Azure resource ID of the disk encryption set used to encrypt the managed OS disk.
